title: Open extension commutes with the canonical scheme/Galois comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the finite coefficient ring $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, with $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $n\geq1$, of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an open immersion of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be its base change to $k$, and fix $m\geq1$. Write $\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ and $g_X,g_Y$ for the scheme and geometric Galois Frobenii [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] at $A$. Let $\kappa_{m,X}$ and $\kappa_{m,Y}$ be the comparisons [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], each specified by the factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], canonical pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and absolute-Frobenius trivialization [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ write
$$
b_{\Phi,m,M}:L(\Phi_Y^m)^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!L(\Phi_X^m)^*M,\qquad
b_{g,m,M}:L(g_Y^m)^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!L(g_X^m)^*M
$$
for the canonical exchanges [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] of the Cartesian squares [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]. Then
$$
b_{g,m,M}\circ\kappa_{m,Y,j_!M}=j_!(\kappa_{m,X,M})\circ b_{\Phi,m,M}.
$$
The equality is natural in $M$ and holds for every $m\geq1$.

source.place: Step 2: compatibility of the canonical comparisons with the Cartesian open squares

proof.text:
For $Z=X,Y$ put $H_Z=F_Z^{am}$, where $F_Z$ is absolute $p$-power Frobenius, and write $P_Z=L\Phi_Z^{m*}$, $G_Z=Lg_Z^{m*}$, $T_Z=LH_Z^*$. These schemes have characteristic $p$, since their structure maps factor through $k_0$ of characteristic $p$. By [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] and [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $H_Z=g_{\sigma,Z}^m\Phi_Z^m$ and $g_Z=g_{\sigma,Z}^{-1}$, hence $\Phi_Z^m=g_Z^mH_Z$. Let $c_Z:P_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}T_ZG_Z$ be canonical pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Write $t_Z:T_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ for the $am$-fold trivialization [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. The specified comparison [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] is exactly
$$\kappa_{m,Z,N}=t_{Z,G_ZN}\circ c_{Z,N}.$$
This uses the geometric inverse of arithmetic Frobenius; neither $g_Z$ nor $H_Z$ is required to be a $k$-morphism.

source.place: Step 2: expand the specified comparison using scheme-galois-comparison.proof.md, first displayed construction

proof.text: We fix the coherence of the canonical pullback comparisons used below. The finite constant coefficient identifications preserve constants by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], so all composites use those same identifications. The explicit comparison of [lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit] sends $(v\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $v\otimes c_h(a)b$. For three pullbacks both reassociations therefore send $((v\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes d$ to $v\otimes c_hc_k(a)c_h(b)d$; the underlying fibre-product reassociations have the same projections. Thus these comparisons agree, including when one map is the open inclusion. Restricting the formula to the open keeps precisely the same sections and scalar multiplication, so also gives that comparison there. Pullbacks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; applying the formulas degreewise and descending by clauses (2),(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] preserves these equations. They give the canonical derived comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], whose statement specifies the same termwise comparison on K-flat representatives. Hence reassociating pullbacks before or after restriction gives the same map.

source.place: Step 2: elementary coherence calculation for the canonical comparisons used to restrict the factorization

proof.text:
Put $r=Lj^*$. The commutative squares [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] give canonical composition comparisons
$$\alpha_P:rP_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}P_Xr,\qquad \alpha_G:rG_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Xr.$$
Absolute Frobenius commutes with $j$, and [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback], applied to $u=j$ and $b=am$, gives $\alpha_T:rT_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Xr$ and the precise equality
$$t_{X,rN}\circ\alpha_{T,N}=r(t_{Y,N}).$$
That node identifies $t_Z$ with the trivialization of Step 1, including its iterates; $A$ is a finite commutative ring, as required. The coherence calculation in Step 2, applied to $\Phi_Z^m=g_Z^mH_Z$, gives
$$c_{X,rN}\circ\alpha_{P,N}=T_X(\alpha_{G,N})\circ\alpha_{T,G_YN}\circ r(c_{Y,N}).$$
Every term has source $rP_YN$ and target $T_XG_XrN$.

source.place: Step 2: restriction compatibility of the absolute-Frobenius trivialization, using the explicit pullback-naturality interface

proof.text:
Expand $\kappa$ by Step 1 and use Step 3. Naturality of $t_X$ with respect to $\alpha_{G,N}$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{m,X,rN}\circ\alpha_{P,N}
&=t_{X,G_XrN}\circ T_X(\alpha_{G,N})\circ\alpha_{T,G_YN}\circ r(c_{Y,N})\\
&=\alpha_{G,N}\circ t_{X,rG_YN}\circ\alpha_{T,G_YN}\circ r(c_{Y,N})\\
&=\alpha_{G,N}\circ r(\kappa_{m,Y,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the restriction identity for the specified comparisons, rather than for an unspecified isomorphism between the two pullback functors.

source.place: Step 2: substitution of the construction of kappa and naturality of its absolute-Frobenius trivialization

proof.text:
Use the derived open units $u_Q:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}rj_!Q$ from [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], with inverses $
u_Q$. The squares in [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] are Cartesian, so [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] supplies $b_P=b_{\Phi,m,M}$ and $b_G=b_{g,m,M}$. Its identity normalization on the open means exactly
$$
u_{P_XM}\circ r(b_P)=P_X(
u_M)\circ\alpha_{P,j_!M},\qquad

u_{G_XM}\circ r(b_G)=G_X(
u_M)\circ\alpha_{G,j_!M}.$$
These equalities use the canonical composition comparisons fixed in Step 2 and the open units; the normalization theorem uses those same units. All functors here act on the ordinary derived categories of pro-etale modules with constant coefficient $A$. Thus its derived-unit assertion applies directly, without passing to an etale category or testing on geometric stalks.

source.place: Step 2: use the identity normalization of the two canonical open-square exchanges

proof.text:
Write $L=b_G\circ\kappa_{m,Y,j_!M}$ and $R=j_!(\kappa_{m,X,M})\circ b_P$. Apply Step 4 with $N=j_!M$, and then naturality of $\kappa_{m,X}$ for $\nu_M:rj_!M\to M$. Step 5 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\nu_{G_XM}\circ r(L)
&=G_X(\nu_M)\circ\alpha_{G,j_!M}\circ r(\kappa_{m,Y,j_!M})\\
&=G_X(\nu_M)\circ\kappa_{m,X,rj_!M}\circ\alpha_{P,j_!M}\\
&=\kappa_{m,X,M}\circ P_X(\nu_M)\circ\alpha_{P,j_!M}\\
&=\kappa_{m,X,M}\circ\nu_{P_XM}\circ r(b_P)
=\nu_{G_XM}\circ r(R).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is naturality of the open-unit inverse $\nu$. Since $\nu_{G_XM}$ is invertible, $r(L)=r(R)$.

source.place: Step 2: explicit calculation of the restrictions of both sides of the claimed equality

proof.text: The derived full faithfulness of $j_!$ in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] now lifts this equality. Indeed precompose $L,R$ with $b_P^{-1}$, obtaining maps $f,h:j_!P_XM\to j_!G_XM$. Full faithfulness writes them uniquely as $j_!f_0,j_!h_0$. Naturality of $\nu$ gives $f_0=\nu_{G_XM}\,r(f)\,u_{P_XM}$ and the same formula for $h_0$. Their restrictions agree by Step 6, hence $f_0=h_0$, $f=h$, and $L=R$. The comparisons of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] and the exchanges of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] are natural in the coefficient complex, so both sides are natural in $M$. The argument was for an arbitrary $m\geq1$ and used $am$ throughout, proving every asserted iterate, without any induction or extra Weil structure on $M$.

source.place: Step 2: lift restriction equality by full faithfulness of derived open extension and conclude naturality

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q155-f018a7aae (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and every cited statement. I also read the parent's citing step, the blueprint (main-20261015) prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator proof Step 2, and the blueprint_update construction of kappa in prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison. The delivery has no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. Statement checks: g_X and g_Y are the geometric Frobenius g_gamma = g_sigma^{-1}, the same as in lem-trf-frobenius-open-square. The coefficient category is the ordinary D(Z_proet, A) with A = O_E/varpi^n, which is annihilated by l^n with l != p. Both squares are Cartesian by lem-trf-frobenius-open-square, and b goes Lh^*j_! -> j_!Lh^*, the direction of lem-trf-open-square-exchange. X_0 is of finite type because it is open in the noetherian Y_0. Step 1: Fr^{(q^m)} = g_sigma^m Phi^m, so Phi^m = g^m F^{am}; I checked this on sections and on Spec k_0. kappa = t∘c is exactly the specified construction. Step 2: I recomputed both reassociations from the local formula of lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit and got v⊗c_h c_k(a) c_h(b) d both times. Exactness and clause (3) of the localization node carry the equality to the derived category. Step 3: lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback with u = j, b = am gives the restriction equation, and its trivialization is the same iterate as in Step 1. Steps 4 to 7: I recomputed every composite and its types. The naturality of t, the two normalization equations, cancelling the invertible nu, and the full-faithfulness lift through b_P^{-1} all hold. Edge cases j = id, X_0 empty, M = 0 and m = 1 behave correctly. Duplicate search: no node in the DAG or the blueprint states this square; lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator gives only the exchange b_m, without kappa. I accept the declared tool_uses: each is a coherence interface that the item's statement or the blueprint's Step 2 already prescribes. No SGA source is used and no fixes were written.
